what: tools/corr.js: the same-game correlation table's measurement (every key's observations, its four outcomes [neither, second only, first only, both], rho by maximum likelihood, its jackknife and iid errors, the shrink and the shrunk value, and the value shipped after the positive definite repair), the threshold check and the validation on a season the development table never saw

win.note: the closing moneyline's own chance, unshifted
the closing moneyline's own chance, unshifted

thresholdCheck.what: rho at lines where the over is about 30% (a milestone above the main line) beside rho at the main line, development seasons, the main kinds (refused pairs left out)

validation.what: the development table (2023-2025, repaired as shipped) on 2026, which it never saw: the joint hit rate of every two-leg combination the builder could join (refused pairs left out; a double-, triple-double or milestone is Yes only), as the copula says, as the plain product (independence) says, and as happened; log loss of the combination hitting (lower is better), copula minus independence, its paired 90% interval resampling games; byLift groups the combinations by the copula's joint over the product

psd.note: every leg one game can carry (13 players a side, every kind each, the win, the cover and the total): positive definite as written, so every set of legs the builder can join is (a principal submatrix of a positive definite matrix is one)

hold.formula: a game's legs pay min(their decimal prices multiplied, HOLD / J), J the copula's joint chance of the legs' implied chances (each price's own 1 / decimal, margin left in) at this table's rho; legs of different games multiplied as before
hold.basis: the NFL hub's SGP_HOLD (props/build/part3.js), fitted to two real DraftKings same-game tickets on Detroit at Buffalo, 2026-09-17: the correlated leg prices gave 7.33 and 5.36 where DraftKings offered 6.25 and 5.05, cuts of 0.852 and 0.942, 0.896 their geometric mean
hold.untested: no DraftKings same-game price is recorded anywhere this hub reads (ESPN's feed carries none), so the hold is the NFL's, untested on the NBA: the price it gives is an estimate and is shown as one
